messages:
elaine: quick heads-up — i sketched a compact rewrite for how we store per-route quotas in console_quotas to reduce cold queries and disk usage. want quick vet before i start a backfill
raf: sketch? link to schema or example rows?
elaine: gist -> https://gist.github.com/redwood/compact-quota-proposal (TL;DR: collapse per-interval rows into a single compact payload + an indexed summary row)
sanjay: curious about read patterns. dashboards currently query p99/counter by route/date window — will that still be efficient?
elaine: yes, summary row keeps aggregate counters and a JSONB 'buckets' payload for occasional deep-dive. primary read path hits summary only.
katie: how about quota gating for realtime checks (api quota enforcement)? we need a cheap lookup path for token validation.
elaine: enforcement will still read a lightweight view: quota_index(route_id, window_start) with precomputed allowed/tokens_used. full payload is for console & analytics only
raf: sounds OK. what about telemetry/metrics? we need stable field names for dashboards & alerts
elaine: plan: emit a compatibility telemetry field 'quota_shape_v2' during dual-write window. dashboards keep querying quota_shape_v1 until we cutover
sanjay: dual-write is meh for backfills — expensive. can we instead write adaptors in the read layer for a transition period?
elaine: read-adaptor approach considered. downside: complexity across console and analytics consumers. dual-write gives signal that both sides see equivalent data
katie: is there a proposed backfill strategy? last time a full reindex burned iops
elaine: proposing incremental backfill across route_id ranges + sampling with a bloom-filter pre-pass to avoid rewriting unchanged rows. pseudocode:
```
-- pre-pass: compute changed route_ids
CREATE TEMP TABLE candidate_routes AS
SELECT route_id FROM console_quotas WHERE hash(route_id) % 1000 = $shard;
-- bloom pass offline: mark if compact_repr != current_compact_repr
-- then backfill candidates only
```
raf: bloom filter idea neat — saves churn. do we have code for that bloom pass?
migrator-bot: scheduled job created: quota-compact-bloom-pass/shard-0 queued for 2026-04-02T03:00:00Z
sanjay: what about analytics joins? the analytics pipeline expects one row per interval per route for timeseries aggregation. packed buckets will break that downstream
elaine: agreed. plan is to keep an envelope table console_quotas_timeseries that we fill via a transform job (unpack buckets into timeseries) during migration. consumers can switch to reading consolidated summary or the timeseries projection depending on SLAs
katie: timeline?
elaine: phased: (1) add compact schema + dual-write hooks (2 weeks), (2) start bloom pre-pass + incremental backfill (3 weeks), (3) enable timeseries projection and run canary queries (1 week), (4) flip dashboards and leave read-adaptor in place for 2w then deprecate
raf: does this require any router changes? i.e., policy eval for quota enforcement — must be zero-downtime
elaine: no router changes. enforcement reads the index view which we'll maintain during dual-write. we’ll publish a contract doc for the enforcement API
sanjay: canary plan? how do we validate correctness at scale?
elaine: canary on 5% of routes (low-traffic) and cross-check tokens_used against v1 counts. alerts if divergence > 0.5% for 1h
katie: dashboard UX: need a flag to let product opt into seeing compact view; UX will need migration notes
raf: audit logs? customers will ask for migration auditability
elaine: include a migration_audit table with row-level mapping old_row_id -> new_compact_id + checksum + migrated_at
migrator-bot: backfill job started shard=0 (eta ~ 6h). logs: https://ci.redwood.run/jobs/quota-backfill-shard-0/6678901234
sanjay: rollback story?
elaine: rollback is to pause canary, run reverse transform (unpack compact into timeseries using migration_audit), and flip reads back to v1. must keep dual-write for at least 48h post-canary
katie: ok. please add a console migration banner for admins and an opt-out toggle for enterprise customers
elaine: will do. any objections to go ahead with PR for schema + dual-write hooks?
raf: +1 from infra side, watch the backfill iops cap
sanjay: +1 from analytics—please include timeseries projection tests
katie: +1 from console product, coordinate with UX on banner copy
elaine: thanks all — i'll open PR tonight and tag reviewers.
